newsitem.title: USA: Senate defeats a "partial birth" ban alternative.
newsitem.headline: Senate defeats a "partial birth" ban alternative.

text.p: U.S. Senators on Thursday easily defeated a bill backed mostly by liberal Democrats that would have restricted late term abortions but would not have banned so-called "partial birth" abortions.

By a 72-28 vote, the Senate defeated a measure sponsored by California Democrat Sen. Dianne Feinstein. It would have limited abortions late in pregnancy, with exceptions "to avert serious adverse health consequences to the woman." The Senate is to vote later Thursday on another measure that has a more narrowly worded health exemption.
A critic of Feinstein's bill, Tennessee Republican Bill Frist, said the health language "is a huge exception people will drive through to potentially more abortions than are done today."

The vote is likely to be closer Thursday night on the separate alternative offered by Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota. That bill, backed by some Republicans who favor abortion rights, would ban abortions after a fetus is viable, or capable of surviving outside the womb. It allows exemptions for women facing "grievous" physical health risks.

Pennsylvania Republican Rick Santorum, chief sponsor of a bill that would ban all "partial birth" abortions before or after viability, has enough votes to pass his bill but not the 67 needed to withstand a promised veto by President Bill Clinton.
The procedure, also referred to as dilation and extraction, involves the partial extraction of the fetus feet-first, the subsequent suctioning out of the fetal brain and the removal of the fetus.
